chunks.text:
What if I'm getting an error message that my account can't be linked?

Please reach out to our learner support team to resolve the error: https://learner.coursera.help/hc (opens in new tab).

Learner Guide

A short help document provided by Texas Tech that explains how to enroll, link accounts, use the Industry Career Certificates program, and where to get help.

Learner support team

Coursera’s help team who assist with account linking, verification, access problems, and other issues related to Coursera courses and certificates.

Learning history

A record of courses, progress, and certificates associated with a user account on a learning platform.

Learning program / learner program

A group or collection of courses or certificates an organization (like TTU) provides to its learners through Coursera.

How can I get more help from Coursera?

Visit https://learner.coursera.help (opens in new tab). It has a lot of articles to answer your most common questions. You can also make sure you are logged into your account to start a live chat with one of the Coursera Learner Support agents, available 24/7. You also can refer to the Learner Guide shared by the admins from your organization.

How can I link my personal account if I don't remember my password?

Reset your password by going to Coursera reset password (opens in new tab) and then follow the process to link your accounts.

What if I already have a Coursera account?

If you already have an account with your personal email, you can link it with your official account to maintain a single learning history.

Detailed steps for linking: may be found at https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/115001710066-Join-a-learning-program (opens in new tab)

What is a time ticket?

This is a specific date and time window that is assigned to you that will allow you to register for classes. You can find your Time Ticket by following the steps below:

Step 1: Login to Raiderlink (opens in new tab)

Step 2: Navigate: Find and click on the "Add or Drop Classes" tool.

Step 3: Click on “View Information”, this will show you your time ticket.

*If you cannot locate your time ticket or have an enrollment issue, contact your Online Student Advocate for assistance. You may also need to check for and resolve any "holds" on your account that could prevent registration.

What are peer-reviewed assignments?

Peer-reviewed assignments are graded by learners who are also taking the certificate at the same time. In order to receive a grade, you typically need reviews with a passing score from 3 peers on your assignment submission and also need to review the assignments of 3 peers in order to complete the assignment. Please note that receiving peer reviews often takes time (up to 1-2 weeks or sometimes longer), as it depends on the number of available reviewers in the course as well as your submission being in circulation long enough. Please take this into account and allow enough time to meet any deadlines to complete courses.

What do I do if the Coursera platform is asking me for payments?

This means you are not viewing the certificate through your Texas Tech’s learning program. Make sure you access Coursera Career Academy through your Industry Career Certificates link shared by your organization and then navigate to your desired certificate. If you are on the Coursera consumer site, you will be asked for payment. You can double-check that by clicking on the toggle in the top left corner and you will see a dropdown with the list of all the programs you are a part of (My Coursera means Coursera consumer site). If you do not see the dropdown toggle, that means you have not joined any learning programs.

Why am I not receiving any emails from Coursera?

You must verify your email address in order to receive the emails. You will receive an email to verify your account, please click on the same to verify. If you’re not able to verify, then reach out to our learner support team at https://learner.coursera.help/hc (opens in new tab).

How is this different from signing up on coursera.org?

Texas Tech has partnered with Coursera to provide access to the Career Academy certificates to our students at no charge. When you create an account on coursera.org, you are accessing the consumer site and will be asked to pay for the program. When you join the program specifically created for Texas Tech using your Texas Tech University email, you can access the Career Academy certificates at no charge.

How can I schedule an appointment with my Online Student Advocate?

Step 1: Login to Raider Success Hub (opens in new tab) with your eRaider credentials.

Step 2: On the homepage, you will see the option “Schedule an Appointment”.

Step 3: The scheduling wizard will walk you through the process of making an appointment, selecting the type of appointment you wish to make such as: course planning, degree exploration, etc.

Step 4: Recently viewed Success Team members will auto-populate the first screen, and you'll have the ability to search for other Success Team members using the search tool.

Step 5: After choosing an available Success Team member, you'll be asked to choose a topic to meet about.

Step 6: The next two screens provide details on the availability of the Success Team member and allow you to choose a date and time for the appointment as well as the modality of the appointment (in-person, phone, online).

Step 7: After confirming the details, the appointment is set!

Would Online+ be better for me since I work full time and I cannot attend class in person? Can I take all my classes online from the beginning of college?

The Texas Tech Online+ program is designed specifically for working professionals, providing the flexibility to complete your coursework fully online. This makes it an excellent choice for individuals who work full-time and cannot attend classes in person. You can take all your classes online from the beginning of your studies, as the program offers various online degree options that can accommodate your schedule. If you're interested in learning more or getting started with the Online+ program, please visit http://GoOnline.ttu.edu (opens in new tab) or contact them directly at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

My Coursera

The personal view of the Coursera consumer site. If you see “My Coursera,” you are on the public Coursera site (not the organization-sponsored program) and may be asked to pay for content.

Name verification

A check to confirm a learner’s real name. If name verification is pending, certificate issuance may be delayed until the learner completes the verification steps.

I was already admitted - what happens now?

Admitted students will receive specific instructions early March outlining:

Step 1: How to transition into the Online+ model

Step 2: Next enrollment steps

Step 3: Any required actions

Are there any limitations on transfer credits?

This program requires a blended delivery format. All coursework is completed online, but students are required to attend an on-campus new student orientation session and three (3) summer professional development sessions.

Qualified applicants should have full-time professional experience in either a public or private two-year or four-year higher education institution or state or federal educational agency serving higher education. Applicants must show a clear connection to higher education.

Doctor of Philosophy in Personal Financial Planning

Texas Tech's personal financial planning Ph.D. program enjoys a national reputation for excellence, so your work will draw serious attention from journal editors, conference programmers, and industry professionals.

Our financial planning doctoral program stands out for its:

Step 1: World-class faculty. You will work with leading authorities in personal financial planning. Texas Tech has the nation's largest personal financial planning faculty, with experts in a broad range of specialties.

Step 2: Outstanding career outcomes. Graduates from our personal financial planning program have earned tenure-track faculty placements throughout the U.S., including numerous departmental leadership positions. In addition, many graduates have used the Ph.D. as a springboard to non-academic careers in financial planning or entrepreneurship.

Step 3: Rigorous theoretical foundation. You will examine the most current research in personal financial planning, including specialized aspects such as the psychology of financial planning, behavioral finance, risk management, and household economics.

Step 4: Practical training in research and teaching. Our Ph.D. students get practical training and mentorship in teaching and research from the top researchers in the field and well-established practitioners. This guidance strengthens your curriculum vita and makes you the ideal candidate for faculty positions or industry careers.

Why did I not get my certificate when I completed the non-credit course?

This could happen because of the following reasons:

1. Pending name verification

2. Pending identity verification ( ID verification ) (this is required for only a few courses and you would need to upload a valid ID proof)

3. Please note that there are select courses that do not offer a certificate.

Why would I be placed on probation if I have never withdrawn from a course and my GPA is higher than 2.0?

Probation status can depend on academic program factors beyond just withdrawing from courses or maintaining a GPA above 2.0. Each institution may have specific policies related to academic probation that consider factors such as overall academic performance, course completion rate, or adherence to university guidelines. It would be beneficial to contact your Online Student Advocate or consult the academic policies laid out by Texas Tech University for clarification on your specific situation regarding probation. For any personalized inquiries, you can reach out to Texas Tech Online+ at online@ttu.edu or call 1-844-691-0494.

How do I get enrolled?

After applying and being admitted, you will work with an academic advisor and your Online Student Specialist.

Online Master of Professional Accounting

Launch your accounting career and meet CPA exam requirements with Texas Tech’s fully online Master of Professional Accounting. This 30-hour program builds core accounting expertise and prepares you for professional practice and licensure success.

The Online Master of Professional Accounting (MPAcc) at Texas Tech University is a 30-credit-hour graduate program launching in fall 2026, designed for students without an undergraduate accounting degree who want to pursue professional accounting careers and satisfy CPA exam requirements. The curriculum maps to core content areas tested on the CPA exam — including Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR), Auditing and Attestation (AUD), Taxation and Regulation (REG) and Information Systems and Controls (ISC) — while developing technical proficiency and professional competencies needed in public accounting, industry and non-profit environments. Students study taxation, auditing, accounting information systems, advanced accounting topics, ethics and business law. Delivered fully online and asynchronously, the program provides flexibility for working professionals and prepares graduates to excel as accounting practitioners, leaders and strategic contributors in a wide range of organizations.

Introduction

We welcome you to Texas Tech online. Below are some of the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ's) that we receive for Registration.

How do I switch from in person to 100% online?

Switching to 100% online from in person , Go to Raiderlink , then student dashboard under the registrar tab on right side , fill out form Transition to 100% online , this is a separate formal application that can be denied.

Graduate Enrollment Status (8-Week Model)

Step 1: Full-time: 6 credit hours

Step 2: Half-time: 3–5 credit hours

Step 3: Less than half-time: 1–2 credit hours

Students typically take 1–2 courses per 8-week term depending on their enrollment status and goals.

Online Student Advocates and Advisors can guide students in selecting an appropriate course load.

How do I withdraw from my coursework?

Students should always check-in with their Online Student Advocate. A review of the Academic and Financial Calendars to determine if there are any consequences of withdrawal is encouraged, along with contacting:

Step 1: Student Business Services (opens in new tab)

Step 2: Financial Aid (opens in new tab), Military & Veterans Office (opens in new tab) for individualized help

Step 3: Login to Raiderlink (opens in new tab)

Step 4: Click on “My Student Dashboard"

Step 5: Click on “Registrar Forms"

Step 6: Click on “New Registrar Request”

Step 7: Click on “Student Withdraw”

Step 8: Remember to withdraw only from the specific term you wish to drop to zero hours (ex. You wish to drop out of Early Fall, make sure you are enrolled in Late Fall first). Then select the Early Fall term on the Withdraw form.

Step 9: For more information, please visit TTU Registrar Office (opens in new tab).

Prior to dropping or withdrawing from any course, students should always discuss the financial consequences of dropping or withdrawing with their financial aid advisor.

How does financial aid work in 8-week terms?

Financial aid eligibility is based on enrollment status within the academic period.

Enrollment Status for Financial Aid:

Step 1: Full-time: 6 credit hours

Step 2: Half-time: 3–5 credit hours

Step 3: Less than half-time: 1–2 credit hours

Aid eligibility and disbursement may vary depending on enrollment level. Students should be referred to the Financial Aid Office for individualized guidance.

What is considered "full-time" for 8-week courses?

Full-time status is 6 hours each 8-week term.

answer.text:
If you're having trouble accessing your digital textbooks despite clearing your cache, trying different browsers, and using different devices, consider the following steps:

- **Check Internet Connection**: Ensure you have a stable internet connection, as connectivity issues can affect access to online resources.

- **Verify Login Credentials**: Double-check that you are using the correct login credentials for the platform hosting your digital textbooks.

- **Update Software**: Make sure your browser and any relevant apps are up to date, as outdated software can cause compatibility issues.

- **Disable Browser Extensions**: Sometimes, browser extensions can interfere with website functionality. Try disabling them to see if it resolves the issue.

- **Contact Technical Support**: If the problem persists, reach out to the technical support team of the platform where your digital textbooks are hosted. They can provide specific assistance and troubleshoot further.

For issues related to Coursera, you can visit their support page at [https://learner.coursera.help/hc](https://learner.coursera.help/hc) for more help or to start a live chat with their support agents.

Online Advanced School Counseling Certificate

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. This 12-hour graduate certificate is delivered 100% online through asynchronous coursework and provides the specialized preparation required for Texas School Counselor certification.

The curriculum develops the knowledge and skills necessary to support the academic, career, personal, and social development of K–12 students. Students learn to design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive school counseling programs; collaborate with educators, families, and community partners; advocate for equitable student outcomes; and provide developmentally appropriate counseling services within school settings.

The certificate includes the coursework and supervised practicum required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for certification. Candidates complete a 160-hour supervised practicum in an approved Texas K–12 school setting under the supervision of a qualified school counselor and in accordance with Texas Tech University’s Educator Preparation Program (EPP) requirements.

This certificate is intended for individuals who already hold a master’s degree in counseling and wish to expand their professional practice into the K–12 educational setting without completing an additional master’s degree.

Completion of the certificate satisfies the educational and practicum requirements for Texas School Counselor certification through Texas Tech University’s approved Educator Preparation Program. Candidates must also meet all applicable Texas Education Agency certification requirements, including passing the required certification examination and any additional state requirements in effect at the time of application for certification.

query.raw: If a transcript still shows "in progress" even after the course is finished, why does that happen?

chunks.text:
What happens if I have fewer than 80 credit hours?

Students with 70–79 credit hours can still enroll, but the total cost may exceed $10,000 (usually still under $15,000).

Students with 60–69 credit hours may qualify for a different Texas Tech degree program, or work with an advisor to develop a plan utilizing community college courses or self-paced courses to get to 70 transferable hours

Students with fewer than 60 credit hours should speak with an advisor to discuss alternative options.

This program is specifically for students who already have significant prior college credits.

answer.text:
To find out if you missed the graduation application deadline as a graduate student at Texas Tech University, you should contact the Registrar's Office or your academic advisor. They can provide the most accurate and up-to-date information regarding deadlines and any necessary steps you need to take.

For questions about the commencement ceremony, you can reach out to the commencement office or check the university's official commencement webpage for details.

If your transcript still shows "in progress" even after a course is finished, it could be due to:

- **Grade Submission Delay**: The instructor may not have submitted final grades yet.
- **Processing Time**: There might be a delay in updating the course status from "in progress" to "completed" by the registrar's office.
- **Administrative Holds**: There could be holds on your account preventing the update.

For specific inquiries about your transcript status, contact the Registrar's Office for assistance. They can provide detailed information and help resolve any issues with your transcript.

For further assistance, you can contact TTU Online at 1-844-691-0494 or email online@ttu.edu.

Would Online+ be a good fit for someone that did not finish high school but got their GED?

Online+ may be an option if you have obtained a GED. We require an official high school transcript for any high school coursework completed before obtaining your GED. Official transcripts must be sent directly from the high school to Texas Tech University to Admissions.Transcripts@ttu.edu if sent electronically. Transcripts may take several business days to be downloaded, received, and processed by Texas Tech University. GED scores can be emailed to the student’s Enrollment Service Specialist for the application.

Online Advanced School Counseling Certificate

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. This 12-hour graduate certificate is delivered 100% online through asynchronous coursework and provides the specialized preparation required for Texas School Counselor certification.

The curriculum develops the knowledge and skills necessary to support the academic, career, personal, and social development of K–12 students. Students learn to design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive school counseling programs; collaborate with educators, families, and community partners; advocate for equitable student outcomes; and provide developmentally appropriate counseling services within school settings.

The certificate includes the coursework and supervised practicum required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for certification. Candidates complete a 160-hour supervised practicum in an approved Texas K–12 school setting under the supervision of a qualified school counselor and in accordance with Texas Tech University’s Educator Preparation Program (EPP) requirements.

This certificate is intended for individuals who already hold a master’s degree in counseling and wish to expand their professional practice into the K–12 educational setting without completing an additional master’s degree.

Completion of the certificate satisfies the educational and practicum requirements for Texas School Counselor certification through Texas Tech University’s approved Educator Preparation Program. Candidates must also meet all applicable Texas Education Agency certification requirements, including passing the required certification examination and any additional state requirements in effect at the time of application for certification.

What are peer-reviewed assignments?

Peer-reviewed assignments are graded by learners who are also taking the certificate at the same time. Online Advanced School Counseling Certificate

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. This 12-hour graduate certificate is delivered 100% online through asynchronous coursework and provides the specialized preparation required for Texas School Counselor certification.

The curriculum develops the knowledge and skills necessary to support the academic, career, personal, and social development of K–12 students. Students learn to design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive school counseling programs; collaborate with educators, families, and community partners; advocate for equitable student outcomes; and provide developmentally appropriate counseling services within school settings.

The certificate includes the coursework and supervised practicum required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for certification. Candidates complete a 160-hour supervised practicum in an approved Texas K–12 school setting under the supervision of a qualified school counselor and in accordance with Texas Tech University’s Educator Preparation Program (EPP) requirements.

This certificate is intended for individuals who already hold a master’s degree in counseling and wish to expand their professional practice into the K–12 educational setting without completing an additional master’s degree.

Completion of the certificate satisfies the educational and practicum requirements for Texas School Counselor certification through Texas Tech University’s approved Educator Preparation Program. Candidates must also meet all applicable Texas Education Agency certification requirements, including passing the required certification examination and any additional state requirements in effect at the time of application for certification.

Costs vary by program, but Online+ is designed to be competitive and transparent. https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/affordable/.

How much does the 10-K program cost? Are there additional fees?

The total cost is $10,000.00 or less for qualified students. There is a $2,000.00 conversion fee for the 21 hours earned through microcredentials and prior learning experience credits. Students are then billed per credit hour at Texas Tech for remaining course work.

You can get started in the first four micro-credential courses for free and pay later when you convert them to credit.  Also, all eligible prior-learning credits will convert to credit for no cost.

Your advisor will connect you with a financial aid advisor to discuss all financing options.

Can Financial Aid cover the $2,000.00 fee?

The $2,000.00 fee is an out of pocket expense.

Step 1: Affordable – Designed to be completed for $10,000 or less.

They apply economic theory and financial principles to real-world challenges across agricultural production, commodity markets, agribusiness firms, financial institutions and global food systems. Coursework strengthens the ability to evaluate pricing dynamics, manage risk, interpret policy impacts and make data-informed strategic decisions. A dedicated course in generative artificial intelligence for agribusiness introduces emerging technologies that support forecasting, operational efficiency and innovation. Delivered fully online in an asynchronous format, the program offers flexibility for working professionals while maintaining rigorous graduate-level standards. The program is ranked No. 1 in the nation for Online Master’s Degrees in Agricultural Business by Best College Reviews.

Alumni (Texas Tech)

A person who has graduated from Texas Tech University; alumni may have different program access than current students, faculty, or staff.

Online Advanced School Counseling Certificate

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. This 12-hour graduate certificate is delivered 100% online through asynchronous coursework and provides the specialized preparation required for Texas School Counselor certification.

The curriculum develops the knowledge and skills necessary to support the academic, career, personal, and social development of K–12 students. Students learn to design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive school counseling programs; collaborate with educators, families, and community partners; advocate for equitable student outcomes; and provide developmentally appropriate counseling services within school settings.

The certificate includes the coursework and supervised practicum required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for certification. Candidates complete a 160-hour supervised practicum in an approved Texas K–12 school setting under the supervision of a qualified school counselor and in accordance with Texas Tech University’s Educator Preparation Program (EPP) requirements.

What is the 10-k Degree Completion Program?

The 10-k Degree Completion Program is an affordable, hybrid program designed for students with at least 70 transferable college credit hours who want to complete a Bachelor of Science in Leadership Studies or a Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies.

This program requires in-person class attendance twice per month in Texas (DFW or El Paso) to complete the microcredentials (not all courses).

What is the maximum number of credits I can transfer?

You may transfer up to 90 college credit hours, provided that a minimum of 10-degree applicable hours are upper division (3xxx/4xxx) and from a four-year institution,  into the 10k program. If you have more than 90 credits but haven’t earned a degree, you can still apply.

Credits are preliminarily evaluated individually for transfer eligibility; transfer eligibility is subject to change upon admittance to TTU.

Please note Texas Tech does not accept Workforce education or vocational courses as transferable hours. However, student can inquire about a B.A.A.S. degree if the hours are applicable.

What are the main advantages of the 10-K program?

Step 1: Affordable – Designed to be completed for $10,000 or less.

Step 2: Accelerated – Short 4-week courses allow for fast degree completion.

Step 3: Hybrid Learning – Online coursework + in-person support.

Step 4: Personalized Support – Advisors and faculty provide individualized guidance.

Step 5: Designed for Working Adults – Flexible schedule with part-time and full-time options.

Unlike Online Plus, the 10-K program is specifically structured for students completing degrees with prior credits and in-person learning.

How long does it take to complete the 10-K program?

The program can be completed in as little as one year, depending on your prior coursework and study pace.

Each micro-credential course lasts approximately 4 weeks.

What happens if I have fewer than 80 credit hours?

Students with 70–79 credit hours can still enroll, but the total cost may exceed $10,000 (usually still under $15,000).

Students with 60–69 credit hours may qualify for a different Texas Tech degree program, or work with an advisor to develop a plan utilizing community college courses or self-paced courses to get to 70 transferable hours

Students with fewer than 60 credit hours should speak with an advisor to discuss alternative options.

This program is specifically for students who already have significant prior college credits.

Online Advanced School Counseling Certificate

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. This 12-hour graduate certificate is delivered 100% online through asynchronous coursework and provides the specialized preparation required for Texas School Counselor certification.

The curriculum develops the knowledge and skills necessary to support the academic, career, personal, and social development of K–12 students. Students learn to design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive school counseling programs; collaborate with educators, families, and community partners; advocate for equitable student outcomes; and provide developmentally appropriate counseling services within school settings.

The certificate includes the coursework and supervised practicum required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for certification. Candidates complete a 160-hour supervised practicum in an approved Texas K–12 school setting under the supervision of a qualified school counselor and in accordance with Texas Tech University’s Educator Preparation Program (EPP) requirements.

This certificate is intended for individuals who already hold a master’s degree in counseling and wish to expand their professional practice into the K–12 educational setting without completing an additional master’s degree.

Completion of the certificate satisfies the educational and practicum requirements for Texas School Counselor certification through Texas Tech University’s approved Educator Preparation Program. Candidates must also meet all applicable Texas Education Agency certification requirements, including passing the required certification examination and any additional state requirements in effect at the time of application for certification.

The anthropology program reflects the broad scope of the discipline, including the three subfields of archaeology, ethnology, and biological anthropology. International and/or regional field schools in all three areas are highlights of the curriculum, and well-equipped laboratory facilities support faculty and student research in all three subfields.

A student majoring in anthropology must complete 34 semester hours in anthropology, including 10 hours of introductory-level coursework, 3 hours of theory, 9 hours of foundational courses, and 12 hours of electives.

ANTH 2100 (opens in new tab),

ANTH 2300 (opens in new tab),

ANTH 2301 (opens in new tab), and

ANTH 2302 (opens in new tab).

ANTH 3311 (opens in new tab) (human variation) or

ANTH 3310 (opens in new tab) (human evolution);

ANTH 3339 (opens in new tab) (ethnology);

and ANTH 3380 (opens in new tab) (archaeology).

What are peer-reviewed assignments?

Peer-reviewed assignments are graded by learners who are also taking the certificate at the same time. In order to receive a grade, you typically need reviews with a passing score from 3 peers on your assignment submission and also need to review the assignments of 3 peers in order to complete the assignment. Please note that receiving peer reviews often takes time (up to 1-2 weeks or sometimes longer), as it depends on the number of available reviewers in the course as well as your submission being in circulation long enough.
